minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 14, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on November 14, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 10, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed concern with the City’s law firm, Lozano Smith, and Attorney
Bill Curley representing the City and its residents

 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 54956.9: (One case)

 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9): City of Mission Viejo v. State of California, DOF.

City Council Minutes  1  November 14, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed two Closed Sessions matters
dealing with litigation. The Council received an update but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Natasha Sotolongo and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Abraham Cheng.

P2.  Recognize Gayle Wood as a "Home Town Hero"

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation to Gayle Wood, President of the City’s
  Marine Adoption Committee.

P3.  Moulton Niguel Water District Update

  Drew Atwater, Director of Planning for Moulton Niguel Water District, presented
  information on the upcoming rate changes and introduced the MNWD executive team.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Pastor John Steward, M.V.: expressed concern about the possibility of district elections in Mission
Viejo and stated that the aggregate effect will be damaging to the city overall.

Jim Leach, SMWD: presented the City Council with the National Water Reuse Association’s
Customer of the Year award for the Lake Mission Viejo Advanced Purified Water (APW) System.
He said that Santa Margarita Water District appreciates its partnership with the City of Mission
Viejo and the Lake Association.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the Mayor has been disrespectful to public speakers, has
interfered with their 1st Amendment rights and in doing so, has discouraged public participation.

City Council Minutes  2  November 14, 2017
 Felissa Silva, M.V.: announced that Community Choice Energy will bring down utility rates and
will help the residents of Mission Viejo by creating freedom of choice and competition in the
electricity marketplace.

Steve Bell, San Clemente: stated that the City of Mission Viejo has supported Relay For Life like
no other community and has raised more than $3 million over the past 23 years for cancer research
and advocacy. He announced that the 2018 Relay for Life will be held in partnership with five
other cities from June 9 through June 10 at a new location at Mission Viejo’s Oso Viejo
Community Park.

Rudy Padrol, M.V.: thanked the City Council for supporting his business for the 5th year in a row.
He said that Rudy’s Christmas Trees is a fundraising vehicle for 55 non-profit organizations,
including 10 in Mission Viejo. He asked for the City's help to get other businesses involved in his
efforts to support the 2018 Relay for Life.

Ron Ruef, M.V.: mentioned that the “Welcome to Your City Council Meeting” brochure is
outdated and said he is excited for the opening of the new Potocki Center for the Arts off of La
Paz Road.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: thanked the City Council for the spectacular Veterans Day ceremony and
State of the City gala and she commended the City Council and staff for their hard work.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of October 24, 2017, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated October 13, 2017 in the Amount of $2,321,617.26

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 20, 2017 in the Amount of $656,769.14

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  November 14, 2017
 4.  Check Register Dated October 27, 2017 in the Amount of $1,860,312.88

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Claim Against the City - Heirs of Judith Noval

  Rejected claim.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2017

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September 2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for September 2017

  Received and filed.

10.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending September 30, 2017

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  September 30, 2017.

11.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2018 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects and Federal Fiscal Year 2019 Federal
  Transportation Improvement Program Update

  (1) Adopted Resolution 17-53 Approving the Submittal of a Candidate City of Mission
  Viejo Transportation Project to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for
  Funding Consideration Under the OCTA Measure M2 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program for Regional Capacity Projects; and (2) adopted Resolution 17-54
  Certifying that the City of Mission Viejo Has the Resources to Fund the Projects in the
  Federal FY 2018/19-2023/24 Transportation Improvement Program and Affirming Its
  Commitment to Implement All Projects in the Program.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  November 14, 2017
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

12.  Overview of the California Voting Rights Act and Request for Public Input

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:58 p.m., Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed opposition to the idea of district elections and stated that she
  was one of two Hispanics who served on the City Council. She volunteered to participate
  on a committee to look at this matter.

  Ron Ruef, M.V.: announced that he came to the public hearing to listen and gather
  information more than anything else. Mr. Ruef stated that he doesn't like the district
  concept and he supports the current at large election system.

  Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing at 8:02 p.m.

  City Attorney Curley announced that the next public hearing on district elections will be
  held at the November 28, 2017, City Council Meeting.

OLD BUSINESS

13.  Felipe Recreation Center Renovations - (CIP 307/310)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Kristi Bailey, M.V.: shared that her family is impressed with every remodel project done
  in Mission Viejo and she is looking forward to the Felipe Tennis Center renovations to
  bring it up to par with all of the other recreation centers in the City.

  Ron Ruef, M.V.: stated that having served the City on the recreation commission, he feels
  that option 1 should be the only option. He said his only concerns are parking and the
  safety of the kids crossing the street to use the restroom.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve option
  1 (in the staff report) which includes installing both the restroom building and the
  office/meeting room building and the related hardscape elements needed to support the
  new structures. (1) Awarded a contract to Optima RPM, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
  $411,079.20 and issue a Purchase Order; (2) awarded a contract to Public Restroom
  Company in an amount not to exceed $494,994.00 and issue a Purchase Order; (3) adopted
  Resolution 17-55 Amending CIP 307/310 Budgets by $215,000.00 by Transferring Funds
  from Unappropriated Reserves.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  November 14, 2017
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Bucknum

22.  Mission Viejo Olympics Ad Hoc Committee

  Jerry Henberger, M.V.: encouraged the Council to form an Olympics ad hoc committee
  and take the first step in mapping out a strategy for participation in the 2028 Olympics.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to establish a
  Mission Viejo Olympic Ad Hoc Committee to identify and explore opportunities for the
  City to participate in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Bucknum appointed Council Member Goodell, former Mayor and Planning
  Commissioner Robert Breton, and residents Jerry Henberger and Jim Montrella to the Ad
  Hoc Committee. She noted that additional members may be appointed later.

OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

14.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation - (CIP 14325)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to (1) approve
  Contract Amendment No. 6 to Construct 1 One Corp., in an amount not to exceed
  $63,755.20 for unknown field conditions and site modifications and (2) adopt Resolution
  17-56 Amending CIP 14325 Marguerites Aquatics Complex budget by $42,000.00.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

15.  Community Services Funding – Fiscal Year 2017-18

City Council Minutes  6  November 14, 2017
   Community Services Supervisor Leslie McDonald presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs noted that Council Member Raths is on the Board of Directors for
  Patriots and Paws and he will bifurcate a motion so Greg Raths can recuse himself on the
  vote for that organization.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
  the Community Services Commission’s grant funding recommendations for fiscal year
  2017-18, with the exception of Patriots and Paws, and approve the proposed administrative
  revisions to the Council Policy #0300-6- Funding of Community Services Programs
  effective fiscal year 2018-19.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Raths left the dais and departed the room.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve the Community Services Commission’s grant funding recommendation for the
  Patriots and Paws organization for fiscal year 2017-18.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Raths

  Council Member Raths returned to the room.

16.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-57 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule
  Effective November 14, 2017, and the City’s Salary Schedule Effective January 1, 2018.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  November 14, 2017
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief John Abel provided holiday safety cooking tips and announced that he is
  retiring at the end of the year so this will be his last City Council Meeting. He noted that
  he lives in Mission Viejo and it has been a real privilege to work in the City as well.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

18.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

19.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

21.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell outlined his recent activities including a state mandated harassment
training course, a Veterans Day service at El Toro Memorial Park, the City's Veteran’s Day
ceremony, and the State of the City event where a female veteran of the year was honored. He
also attended Moulton Niguel Water District’s turf transformation event and a meeting on sober
living legislation. He said there is overwhelming concern with issues surrounding sober living
homes and there is a lot of action swirling around the topic. Council Member Goodell announced
that the Mission Viejo Nadadores have a new head coach for their diving program, former Olympic
medalist (1984 and 1988) Michelle Mitchell.

City Council Minutes  8  November 14, 2017
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley said that she was pleased to participate as Principal for a day at Reilly
Elementary School and to meet the school’s new Principal. She noted that she has been a big
cheerleader for the Capistrano Unified School District but she also supports Saddleback Valley
Unified School District and has the highest regard for both districts. Council Member Kelley
commended City staff and the Saddleback recreation department for a very successful Hometown
Halloween event. She also attended the El Toro Memorial Park Veterans Day ceremony and
Mission Viejo’s Veterans Day ceremony. She commended Mayor Bucknum on the State of the
City event which was held on Veteran’s Day as well. Council Member Kelley announced that there
will be a Blood Drive on November 20, 2017, from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at
City Hall. She stated that the character quality for the month of November is thankfulness and she
shared a quote from Charles Swindoll: “Life is 10% what happens to me and 90% how I react to
it.” In conclusion, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character movie to
support thankfulness is “Up” and it will be shown on Sunday, November 19 in the Council
Chamber at City Hall.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked City staff for a wonderful Veterans Day event and noted that, as
a veteran himself, he really looks forward to the ceremony every year.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs yielded his time due to the late hour.

Mayor Bucknum

Following up to comments on Veteran’s Day, Mayor Bucknum thanked Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
and Council Member Raths for serving the country in the armed forces and for continuing to serve
the community on the City Council. She announced that she enjoyed being Principal for a Day at
Capo Valley High School and the Council supports all of the City’s schools and doesn’t pick teams
and sides. Mayor Bucknum said the Eagle Scout projects are abundant and the Court of Honor
ceremonies are just amazing. She thanked the Eagle Scouts for the many projects they are doing
in town and said you can drive around and see one almost every weekend. She encouraged
residents to stop and thank the Scouts for doing a project in the City. Mayor Bucknum announced
that she was honored to attend the Marine Corps Ball and to participate with the City's adopted
Marine battalion. She also thanked City staff for a very nice evening at the State of the City gala
and said that the collaboration was terrific and did not go unnoticed. She thanked her colleagues
for attending and stated that supporting the Chamber of Commerce is so important because the
goal is to have really diversified Chamber activities. In closing, Mayor Bucknum reminded
residents that there are a lot of events leading into the holidays and the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee will kick things off with their Gifts and Goodies Boutique on Saturday, November 18
beginning at 8:00 a.m. at the Murray Community Center.

City Council Minutes  9  November 14, 2017
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:44 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 28, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 28, 2017

City Council Minutes  10  November 14, 2017
